dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The two May dealer files accepted every received row and reconciled cash to ledger with zero difference and zero duplicate-source-event flags."
"The 90 West-dealer annual rows have effective dates in the same calendar month as their posting dates; the May rows have effective dates from 1–28 May and post on 31 May."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "My analytical inference is that apparent month-end spikes stem directly from asynchronous batch transmission schedules rather than unauthorized revenue generation or backdating."
"The operations email describes monthly annual-renewal files using the dealer transaction date as effective date and month-end as posting date."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Pipeline Processing Defect: rejected because dealer import log files DF-00020 and DF-00040 in `dealer_import_log.csv` indicate 100% row acceptance with zero error flags and zero duplicate source IDs across all 90 West-dealer annual renewals in `recharges.csv`."
"Subscriber entitlement activation status"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "The single next action is a targeted, read-only query comparing the West-dealer trend by `posted_at` and `effective_event_date`, plus a small entitlement sample."
"Keep restatement on hold pending the result."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Decision: Hold escalation; no accounting restatement or technical remediation is justified on current records."
"If policy requires effective-date reporting or the sample finds failed activation, escalate that specific issue; otherwise close the anomaly as reconciled posting timing."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "all 17 transactions represent verified, unique customer transactions" is stronger than the cited uniqueness and import-reconciliation evidence; those checks do not establish customer entitlement or successful activation.

"with complete bank cash settlement" is not clearly supported by the cited import log and reconciliation fields; reconciliation to the ledger is not necessarily proof of bank settlement for each transaction.
"rather than unauthorized revenue generation or backdating" is directionally plausible, but the evidence does not independently test every unauthorized-revenue or backdating pathway.

The submission treats zero duplicate source-event flags and aggregate reconciliation as sufficient to reject a pipeline defect, although these checks do not rule out downstream event-time transformation or reporting defects.
The recommendation does not explicitly require downstream analytics to use `effective_event_date`; it leaves the correction conditional on an additional policy determination.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst appropriately considered a pipeline defect and revenue manipulation, and preserved entitlement activation and reporting-clock uncertainty. The strongest missed or incompletely tested alternative is that the source imports are financially reconciled but the downstream dashboard is still materially distorted by using `posted_at` instead of `effective_event_date`; aggregate import acceptance and zero reconciliation difference do not rule that out.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run and document the actual duplicate-cash and entitlement-impact checks for all 90 West-dealer annual rows, while explicitly tracing `effective_event_date` through the dashboard/reporting pipeline; do not rely on a small entitlement sample or aggregate reconciliation alone.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South CareDesk tickets fell from 175 in January to 104 in June, while control regions were broadly flat: E 101→102, N 168→170, W 176→169."
"Under legacy routing, South had 219 `case_create` sessions out of 442 legacy South sessions; under NOVA-S1, only 90 of 2,709 sessions reached `case_create`."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The pilot email says sessions ending before authentication are monitored in the technical pilot report rather than CareDesk because no verified customer context exists."
"The recording process changed, so the case-count denominator changed with it."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "New self-service stages balance_check (29.1% of sessions) and pack_info (21.3%) ... representing genuine deflection for authenticated callers."
"I cannot test whether failed-authentication customers contact SkyWave again without a read-only subscriber-level 7-day callback/recontact query."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Decision: Defer national expansion and maintain existing South pilot boundaries."
"Keep national rollout on hold pending the query results."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "The single next action is a read-only subscriber callback reconciliation query evaluating 7-day repeat contacts across all 2,709 NOVA-S1 sessions."
"Which exact terminal stages and outcomes are excluded from the containment denominator?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Apparent complaint reduction is heavily driven by 650 pre-authentication drops and automated ticket-creation suppression rather than verified self-service resolution." The evidence shows 650 sessions ending at `authenticate` and exclusion from the CareDesk view, but does not by itself establish that all were drops, complaints, customer friction, or automated suppression.

"The 650 pre-authentication drops ... represent uncaptured customer friction rather than successful self-service resolution." They are not evidence of successful resolution, but abandonment is not itself proof of complaint or friction; the submission should state this as an unresolved hypothesis.

"Analysis ... confirms that the apparent drop is an artifact of measurement changes." The measurement-change explanation is strongly supported, but the available evidence does not fully exclude some genuine improvement from the new authenticated self-service stages.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission appropriately recognizes that balance_check and pack_info may represent genuine authenticated self-service deflection and notes that a low repeat-contact rate could make genuine containment credible. It nevertheless somewhat underplays the benign possibility that some authentication-stage sessions were resolved, intentionally exited, or unrelated to complaints; sampled journey outcomes and call listening are still needed.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Link the 650 authentication-stage sessions to downstream journey outcomes, including repeat contacts, successful recovery, eventual case creation, and a sample of call recordings, while explicitly separating abandonment from complaint. This would test both the missing-case-creation mechanism and the possibility of genuine resolution.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv`, rows 1–4, and names the specific fields `impact_mw`, `cleared`, `event`, `severity`, `duration_min`, `timestamp_local`, and `inverter_id`.
It distinguishes the observed four-row extract from the broader plant record by stating that it lacks an unfiltered baseline and extraction parameters.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It cross-checks severity, clearance status, duration, recurrence by inverter, and impact rather than treating `COMM_LINK_WARN` as proof of equipment failure.

It tests the main damage hypothesis against zero impact, self-clearance, short duration, and one occurrence per inverter, but relies primarily on one event file rather than an independent operational channel.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The conclusion is scoped to the file: 'The four observed events represent isolated, self-resolving occurrences' and explicitly notes that the extract may lack an unfiltered plant baseline.
It gives a clear decision-changing condition: reassess only if the unfiltered query reveals open, critical, recurring, or nonzero-impact events.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: 'Hold escalation and make no equipment change' is proportionate to the reported zero impact and cleared status.
The proposed read-only query without severity/status filters is reversible and discriminates between a benign complete extract and a potentially incomplete or materially worse event set.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: 'Do not escalate any event from this file' accurately reflects the visible evidence while preserving a completeness check.
The submission does not invent a plant problem from the seven-minute communications warning and notes zero MW impact and quick recovery.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: 'The only worthwhile next step is to verify that the export is complete' is a somewhat absolute prioritization; the evidence supports it as the appropriate next step, but not necessarily the only worthwhile one.
'Zero repeat pattern' is valid only within the four-row extract and should not be generalized to the plant without the proposed unfiltered query.
The query described as 'without severity/status filters' may still not establish completeness unless its plant, time-range, pagination, and extraction scope are also verified.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The events could reflect intermittent communications or telemetry-quality issues rather than inverter damage; alternatively, the four-row extract could be incomplete and conceal recurring or impactful events. The submission appropriately treats completeness as the key unresolved uncertainty rather than escalating on the warning label alone.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Specify and execute a reproducible completeness check covering the full plant and date range, including explicit plant/time filters, pagination or row-count validation, and all event statuses and severities; then compare any additional records for impact, recurrence, and open state.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites specific fields and calculations from `dispatch_blocks.csv`, including `base_schedule_mw`, `submitted_schedule_mw`, `actual_mw`, `dsm_rate_rs_kwh`, and `schedule_source`.
It explicitly reproduces the 31.6% calculation: “(662,444.09 - 453,085.88) / 662,444.09 = 31.6%.”
It distinguishes observed arithmetic from inference by labeling the same-day result “descriptive/model-based evidence for that day, not causal proof.”

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The analyst notices the central design issue: “It is a cross-day comparison.”
It constructs the required same-day counterfactual using `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw` on 29 May and calculates the smaller modeled benefit.

It triangulates the dispatch data with the commercial extract and daily variation, and tests alternatives including outcome-informed date selection, fabrication, and the possibility that lower DSM penalty does not imply higher net commercial value.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission states that neither estimate “establishes a general causal effect.”
It gives claim-specific confidence: “High for arithmetic; Medium for causal interpretation.”
It identifies decision-changing unknowns involving pre-outcome selection, immutable timestamps, replication, and complete net settlement rather than relying on a generic request for more data.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation preserves the current pilot while holding national expansion: “maintain the pilot at current scope and run the read-only shadow calculation.”

The proposed prospective validation uses pre-registered matched high-wind stow days, immutable submission timestamps, and net commercial settlement, making it a discriminating and reversible next test.
The action appropriately retains the observed smaller potential benefit rather than treating the pilot as worthless.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately separates “valid arithmetic for two different days” from causal evidence.
It states the correctly scoped same-day result: “about 17.6% below the retained base schedule against the same realized generation.”
It avoids both overclaiming the 31.6% headline and overcorrecting to “no value.”

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The claim that the 28 and 29 May days have “similar listed wind fields” is observational and does not establish similarity in all relevant operating conditions, though the submission appropriately limits its interpretation.
The phrase “stronger same-day modeled estimate” could be read as implying greater causal strength; it is properly qualified elsewhere as single-day, model-based evidence.

The proposed shadow validation may not by itself identify causal impact unless the matched-event design controls for relevant confounders, though the submission correctly calls for pre-registration and replication.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 29 May same-day comparison is genuinely suggestive of pilot value: the submitted schedule produced a modeled penalty about 17.6% below the retained base schedule under the same realized generation. However, block selection, forecast uncertainty, timing, and model assumptions could explain part or all of that difference, so the result supports continued evaluation rather than expansion or dismissal.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Pre-register and execute multiple matched high-wind events with immutable pre-outcome schedule timestamps, while comparing submitted and base schedules block-by-block and reconciling DSM penalties, energy revenue, and pilot costs into net commercial value.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Both share HS6 902110; local suffixes differ."
"Declaration: P1001 declared with 90211000."
"commercial_invoice.pdf confirms P1001, 10 units, CHF 126,900 and air_waybill.pdf links SHP-000522 to CH-2025-000522."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Rejected Hypotheses"
"‘Any differing string proves an error’: rejected because the Swiss reference lists 90211000 and warns Swiss/EU strings need not match."
"‘Helios master data supersedes local declaration filings’: rejected because Helios is commercial data without customs-ruling authority."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "requires Tares confirmation."
"The open question is Swiss legal code on 4 November 2025."
"Swiss code on 2025-11-04 | Effective Tares/ruling | A contradictory code flips decision to escalate; 90211000 closes review."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Helios in product_master_current.xlsx is commercial data, not ruling authority."
"canonical-schema-v0.3.md lacks jurisdiction and version metadata, so direct string comparison cannot prove error."
"Resolving schema deficiencies prevents repetitive false positives across Swiss entries."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible mapping hold and request Tares or ruling confirmation."
"Escalate only if it contradicts 90211000; otherwise close the false positive and add jurisdiction/version/date to the comparator."
"This preserves both options while testing the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "No record contradicts 90211000" is an absence claim that is not fully demonstrable from the listed evidence alone.
"Correct codes from different editions appear as mismatches without discrepancy" is plausible but is stated generally without a cited example or edition comparison.
"CHF 126,900 total closes it" overstates what invoice-value verification can establish; value presentation does not by itself resolve tariff classification.

The assertion that Helios is "without customs-ruling authority" is reasonable from its identification as commercial ERP data, but the submission does not cite a specific authority record or ruling-status field.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss code may have changed or may not apply on 4 November 2025, or a binding Swiss ruling may support a code different from 90211000. That possibility could justify escalation if effective Tares data or a ruling contradicts the matrix row; the submission appropriately identifies and tests this alternative rather than treating the suffix mismatch itself as proof of error.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and cite the effective Swiss Tares or binding-ruling record for 4 November 2025, including its jurisdiction, edition/effective date and product scope, before closing the review.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The 42 HOLD rows are open/right-censored, received 24–30 July, while dispositioned rows were received 22 June–20 July" — specific fields and dates make this traceable, though the conclusion about bias is inferential.

"185 of 262 qcore_release_ts values are exactly 02:10:00" and "The SOP defines the routine target..." — precise, relevant cross-file evidence, but the claimed artifact interpretation is not independently established.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The 45.5-hour figure is a receipt-to-release measure and cannot be relabeled as the SOP target" — correctly separates metric definition from the SOP mechanism.

"the observed 02:10:00 timestamp clustering represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact rather than actual release timing" — plausible mechanism, but stated more strongly than the coincidence and freshness evidence alone supports.
"The main problem is semantic fitness for the KPI, not arithmetic corruption" — appropriately distinguishes data quality from timestamp semantics.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "lab_complete_ts is only a proxy" and "there is insufficient evidence because the required start timestamp is absent" — uncertainty is tied to the missing field and its semantic validity.
"missing/index-pending COA may be source lag rather than confirmed release" — appropriately avoids treating stale status as a proven breach.
"represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact" — insufficiently calibrated as a conclusion rather than a hypothesis requiring validation.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do not launch the ‘one and a half days’ KPI yet" and "Can this extract calculate the SOP's routine evidence-available-to-disposition KPI? No" — directly reframes the decision around the SOP definition.

"Do one read-only validation of 5–10 02:10-stamped batches... before building a dashboard" — small and reversible, but the recommendation would be stronger with explicit acceptance criteria and a primary event-log/evidence-timestamp validation.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "‘The data is broken and should be discarded’: rejected because timestamps... have no negative durations" — tests arithmetic corruption rather than assuming it.
"‘COA MISSING proves release without certificates’: rejected... the extract may lag the portal" — tests a compliance interpretation against freshness evidence.

"‘The 45.5-hour average is the SOP cycle time’: rejected because... required-evidence availability... is not represented" — rejects the key KPI interpretation, although the strongest alternative for 02:10 is not fully tested.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "evidence_available_ts or a validated field mapping for 5–10 batches" — directly requests high-value evidence for the KPI's start event.
"Live QCore audit for a sample of the 185 stamped rows" and "Same-day CertVault/QCore reconciliation" — targeted discriminating tests rather than generic data requests.
The proposed immediate test prioritizes 02:10 validation, while an event/decision timestamp definition or event log is the more central missing evidence for KPI validity.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "the observed 02:10:00 timestamp clustering represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact rather than actual release timing" is an inference presented as established; the artifacts support a strong suspicion and the need for validation, not proof.

"excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours" is potentially misleading because the submission does not define the evidence timestamp or clearly identify the field used for that calculation.

"their omission biases completed-only cycle-time estimates downward" is directionally plausible under right-censoring, but the claim that the HOLD rows are likely the slowest observations should remain conditional until follow-up or survival analysis is performed.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 values could be genuine QCore interface-commit times or a valid operational batch-release convention rather than merely an extract artifact. Even if genuine, they may still measure interface commits rather than decision times; an event log or validated timestamp mapping is needed to distinguish these interpretations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the asserted 02:10 synchronization-artifact conclusion with a quantified hypothesis test using a small sample's QCore audit/event history and, above all, obtain the event or decision timestamp definition for required-evidence availability and disposition before deriving any KPI.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Semantic search is not the real problem" is stronger than the evidence supports: exact MPN joins cover the 13 identified requests but do not establish semantic-search recall or value for the 11 blank-MPN requests.

The label "Actionable now" remains somewhat overstated while the global stock snapshot is stale and live CMMS confirmation has not yet occurred; these are better described as provisionally actionable candidates.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Semantic search may still provide material value for the 11 requests without manufacturer part numbers, even though exact matching performs well for the 13 identified requests. In parallel, temporal inconsistency could invalidate some of the eight provisional matches regardless of retrieval method.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a prioritized live CMMS validation for the eight proposed transfers, checking current unreserved quantity, revision, UOM, qualification, and reservations; record the result as the final gate before calling any candidate actionable.
